cases.title: Crypto Income
names: Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed Al Nahyan
cases.amount_label: Selected 2025 crypto proceeds disclosed by Trump-linked companies
cases.summary: Trump’s annual disclosure records about $1.42 billion across selected crypto royalty, token and equity-sale proceeds. The strongest direct ownership link is CIC Digital: $635.1 million in royalties in a company wholly owned by the trust of which Trump is sole beneficiary. These are identifiable business receipts, with mixed family ownership in other entities; they are not a verified personal net-profit total.
cases.accountability: The president retained a financial interest while his administration shaped cryptocurrency policy. A foreign official’s investment adds a named international counterparty to the money trail.

findings.text: Reuters reported the administration advanced industry-friendly stablecoin rules and reduced crypto enforcement while Trump-family businesses generated crypto income.

WSJ reported that Eric Trump signed a $500 million sale of 49% of World Liberty four days before inauguration; $187 million of the initial installment was directed to Trump-family entities. The buyer was backed by UAE national security adviser Sheikh Tahnoon, who sought U.S. AI chips.
The Block identifies the investment vehicle as Aryam Investment 1. The reported $187 million initial payment must not be added to the annual disclosure’s equity proceeds without reconciliation.

cases.title: Foreign Fees
cases.role: Trump’s son-in-law; Affinity owner; diplomatic adviser
cases.amount_label: Congressional estimate of Affinity’s 2025 foreign-investor fees
cases.period: Calendar 2025; earlier commitment shown as context
cases.status: Estimated firm fees; personal distributions undisclosed
cases.summary: Kushner’s private-equity firm earns management fees from foreign investors while he undertakes diplomacy for his father-in-law. Garcia and Wyden estimated more than $60 million in 2025 fees, including $39 million from Saudi investors. That is a concrete estimate of revenue to the business he owns, not a $2 billion personal gift.
cases.accountability: The issue is the overlap between foreign governments paying an adviser’s business and his influence over U.S. negotiations involving that region. The relationship warrants scrutiny without assuming every foreign investment bought a policy decision.

findings.text: The 2024 Senate letter identifies Kushner as Affinity’s sole owner and describes Saudi PIF’s $2 billion 2021 commitment and fee terms. UAE and Qatari sovereign investors also supplied capital. The $2 billion originated before this study window.
The March 2026 letter explicitly labels its 2025 fee figures as estimates; it does not supply bank-level proof of Kushner’s take-home income.

money.aggregation: Historical context only; not fees or personal wealth

money.aggregation: Crosses start boundary; excluded from in-window total

response.text: Kushner’s October 2026 response disputes the $157 million fee estimate, says fees cover operations, denies using diplomacy to benefit investors, and says he stopped new fundraising conversations when asked to extend his volunteer role. He says outside and White House counsel reviewed compliance.

cases.confidence_basis: Ownership and commercial relationships are identified; the $60 million amount is a named congressional estimate, not an independently audited total. No personal-distribution figure or policy quid pro quo is asserted.
cases.missing_fact: Annual investor-by-investor cash fees, expense deductions, Kushner distributions, and dated conflict-management records; these would turn the current revenue estimate into a reconciled personal-benefit figure.

cases.title: Family Capital
cases.amount_label: Federal loan commitment to a company in his firm’s portfolio
cases.period: Private investment August 2025; OSC announcement November 2025; Commerce award recorded by July 2026
cases.summary: 1789 Capital, where Donald Trump Jr. is a partner, invested in Vulcan shortly before the government announced a $620 million loan commitment for the magnet producer. The public financing can increase the value of a private investment, but the loan is owed by the company; it is not a $620 million payment to Trump Jr.
cases.accountability: This is a traceable route from presidential family connection, through an investment firm, to a federal financing decision. The unresolved financial question is his economic stake and the preferential-treatment question concerns how the financing was initiated and approved.

findings.text: ProPublica reported White House intervention in Vulcan’s financing, citing Pentagon records and interviews.

The August House letter says 1789 bought equity in August 2025 and recounts Maslin’s April 2026 denial that Vulcan benefited from political favoritism. These are the committee’s account and an attributed denial, not a court finding.
Vulcan announced its $65 million Series A in August 2025 and said it was producing magnets; Commerce identified supply-chain and defense applications for the proposed financing.
GAO records a $50 million Commerce direct-funding award to Vulcan by July 15, 2026, with equity provided in exchange. Its table establishes an award, not that all funds were paid.
The announced $700 million OSC financing covered two companies: $620 million for Vulcan and $80 million for ReElement. The combined figure does not replace Vulcan’s amount.

money.personal_allocation: Trump Jr. stake and proceeds not disclosed

money.joint_commitment_context: Vulcan $620 million plus ReElement $80 million made the announced joint $700 million OSC commitment; do not add the joint total to these components.

money.cash_status: GAO records a $50 million award; disbursement not established by Table 1

money.label: Private Series A round
money.personal_allocation: 1789’s participation amount and Trump Jr.’s economics undisclosed

response.text: Maslin told House committee staff that Vulcan had not benefited from political favoritism. The issuer describes an industrial expansion to supply U.S. and allied customers, and Commerce describes domestic supply-chain objectives.

cases.confidence_basis: The partnership, portfolio investment, company-specific OSC commitment and later GAO-recorded Commerce award establish the financial connection. Loan and grant disbursements and Trump Jr.’s individual return remain unpriced.
cases.missing_fact: 1789’s Vulcan stake, Trump Jr.’s partnership ownership and carried interest, loan disbursements, decision chronology and conflict reviews.

editorial_notes: Three cases are ready for reviewable publication with amount types visible beside numbers. Do not place mixed firm receipts, capital commitments and individual proceeds in one personal-benefit ranking.
FY2023–FY2026 denotes the frozen study window, not a claim of complete four-year coverage for each person.
Family edges establish identity only; they do not assign money or wrongdoing. Group-level Trump-family ownership must not be divided among named relatives without evidence.
The Aryam equity sale may overlap the annual disclosure equity proceeds. Keep contextual deal values outside the headline sum.
